assessment_note: Frog-skin bradykinin-related peptides: relaxes rat arterial smooth muscle and targets bradykinin receptors, and its FSAP bradykinin-related subfamily is 12/12 Toxin-keyworded (the July phyllokinin group). The model's Bradykinin-related peptide call is biologically exact; the 'other' ground truth only reflects that the FSAP umbrella collapses to 'other', so this is a label artifact, not a model error.
Potter-wasp venom-gland eumenine mastoparan-EM4, potently hemolytic; MCD family (mastoparan subfamily) is exactly right. The nontox ground truth is a keyword gap.

Jack-jumper-ant venom-gland pilosulin-3 (M-myrmeciitoxin-Mb1a), causes IgE-independent histamine release; UniProt places it in the formicidae venom precursor-01 superfamily, so Formicidae venom family is exactly right.

Bombina skin Maximins 9/H3: maximin-H3 shows strong hemolytic activity and the entry is Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, so tox under the hemolysis rule. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so the model's 'other' is the correct tox call and the nontox label is the error.

Chicken motilin, an endogenous gut hormone acting on the animal's own receptor to drive interdigestive motility. Pharmacological but endogenous, so nontox by the July neuromedin-U / isotocin / motilin ruling. Cationic peptide call -> false positive.
Hornet venom-gland crabrolin: Toxin-keyworded MCD-family mast-cell degranulating peptide, hemolytic on rat and guinea-pig erythrocytes; model called nontox -> false negative.

Tityus serrulatus venom-gland peptide 1; in vivo it diminishes locomotion and induces anxiety in mice, so tox on venom-gland origin plus animal-directed effect. UniProt places it in the NDBP superfamily (short AMP group 4), a modelled class, so Bradykinin-related peptide is the wrong bin.
Russell's viper venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor 4; venom Kunitz-type is exactly right. The nontox ground truth is the usual keyword gap on venom protease inhibitors.

Ascidian defense peptide turgencin-A: no hemolysis assay is reported, but it is directly cytotoxic to human cells (melanoma A2058 IC50 1.4 uM, normal fibroblast MRC-5 IC50 4.8 uM), so tox by extending the hemolysis rule from erythrocyte lysis to animal-cell lysis. THIS IS THE ONE ROW IN THE BATCH RESTING ON THAT EXTENSION rather than on hemolysis proper; revert it to nontox if the rule is meant to stay strictly hemolytic. Turgencin has no UniProt family, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Soapfish skin-secretion grammistin Gs G: ichthyotoxic (LD50 0.19 ug/ml against killifish), hemolytic, cytolytic, Toxin-keyworded; model called nontox -> false negative. Grammistin family is unmodeled, so 'other' would have been the correct call.

Tobacco-budworm virescein, a moricin-family hemolymph AMP of insect innate immunity, not a venom peptide. No hemolysis or cytotoxicity reported, and the moricin family is 0/4 hemolytic, so the hemolysis rule does not reach it. NDBP call -> false positive, the same failure as the July moricins and diapausins.

Bombina skin Maximins 1/H12: Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, and it encodes maximin-1, which has significant cytotoxicity against tumour cell lines and high spermicidal activity. The sibling precursor P83080 (Maximins 1/H1) carries the same maximin-1 and IS Toxin-keyworded, so this nontox label is curator inconsistency. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Ant venom-gland U1-poneritoxin-Ni3d (ponericin-G family); the family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Flannel-moth venom-apparatus U-megalopygitoxin(2)-Mo9, Toxin-keyworded; binary call right, but the caterpillar 2 family is unmodeled ('other' was the label) and Scoloptoxin is a centipede family.
Scorpion venom-gland RK1, a Toxin-keyworded disintegrin-like peptide that blocks tumour-cell proliferation, migration and angiogenesis via integrins; model called nontox -> false negative.

Bombina skin Maximins 4/H3 type 4: maximin-H3 shows strong hemolytic activity and the entry is Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, so tox under the hemolysis rule, even though maximin-4 itself is the mild member of the pair. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Ant venom-gland M-poneratoxin-Dq3a; UniProt bins it in the NDBP superfamily (ponericin-W subfamily), a modelled class, so Formicidae venom family is the wrong axis even though it is genuinely an ant venom peptide. Defensible confusion, not a biological error.

Feather-duster-worm SmCI, a tentacle-crown carboxypeptidase and serine protease inhibitor built from BPTI-Kunitz repeats. No venom apparatus and no animal-directed activity. Venom Kunitz call -> false positive.

Pumpkin-toadlet skin-gland bradykinin-potentiating peptide Brachy: ACE inhibitor, hypotensive, drives NO-mediated vasodilatation in rat tissue, so animal-directed pharmacology (the July phyllokinin precedent). Natriuretic/BPP family is exactly right.
Scorpion venom-gland toxin Tpa3; NDBP superfamily is exactly right. 'Is not toxic to mammals' does not override venom-gland origin, cf. the July secapin ruling.

Bombina skin Maximins 11/H11: maximin-H11 shows strong hemolytic activity (by similarity) and the entry is Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, so tox under the hemolysis rule. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Cone-snail venom-duct conorfamide Tx1.3, a Toxin-keyworded ASIC3 modulator; model called nontox -> false negative. NPY family is unmodeled, hence the 'other' ground truth.
Scorpion venom-gland Css54, hemolytic against human erythrocytes (83% at 25 uM); NDBP superfamily (medium-length AMP group 3) is exactly right.

Human Speedy protein E3, an intracellular testis- and spleen-expressed Speedy/RINGO cell-cycle regulator with no secretion, no annotation and no toxin link. Model called 'other', a confident tox call on a human intracellular protein, so this is the genuinely spurious false positive of this batch (the duck-transferrin analogue).

model_predicted_family: Sea anemone type 1 potassium channel toxin family
assessment_note: Sea-anemone ShK homolog Ask132958, localised to the NEMATOCYST, which is the venom apparatus (the July ShK-like2 versus ShK-like4 discriminator was exactly nematocyte expression). Sea anemone type 1 potassium channel toxin family matches UniProt exactly. Caveat: this homolog has no measurable activity on the Kv channels tested.

Scorpion venom-gland 2.39 kDa venom peptide; not lethal to mice up to 100 ug, but venom-gland origin governs. UniProt assigns no family, and short scorpion toxin superfamily is the taxon-standard bin, so the family call cannot be faulted.
Rattlesnake venom-gland bradykinin inhibitor peptide, a Toxin-keyworded BDKRB2 antagonist; model called nontox -> false negative.

Bombina skin Maximins 5/H4 type 3: maximin-H4 shows strong hemolytic activity and the entry is Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, so tox under the hemolysis rule. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Whip-snake venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor vestiginin-7; venom Kunitz-type is exactly right. Keyword gap on the label side.
Sea-lamprey vasotocin, the endogenous antidiuretic hormone. Vasopressin/oxytocin is the right fold and the wrong biology: the venom-recruited-hormone false positive pattern from July, repeating.
Scorpion venom-gland venom protein 164, an AVIT/prokineticin (MIT1/Bv8-like) venom component; the AVIT family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Flesh-fly SBPI, an endogenous insect trypsin inhibitor with no venom context. Venom Kunitz call -> false positive, the same failure as the July silkworm inhibitor.
Mulga-snake venom-gland basic phospholipase A2 PA-11, LD50 0.24 mg/kg intravenous; Phospholipase family is exactly right. The nontox ground truth is the canonical enzyme keyword gap.
Scorpion venom-gland venom protein 30.1; venom-gland origin makes the tox call right, but UniProt assigns no family and Scoloptoxin is a centipede family, so the family call is unsupported.

Odorranain-A6, an annotation-silent member of the FSAP brevinin subfamily (0/500 Toxin-keyworded, overwhelmingly Antimicrobial-keyworded). The hemolysis rule does not reach it: its own odorranain-A group is 0/47 annotated, so there is no hemolysis evidence to inherit, and the parent brevinin subfamily asserts hemolysis in only 30% of annotated members, which is too weak to impute. Nontox by subfamily inference. Model called 'other', a tox call -> false positive.

Baboon theta-defensin subunit B, an endogenous circular minidefensin of leukocytes; theta-defensins are 0/42 hemolysis-keyworded, so the hemolysis rule does not reach it. The Conotoxin call is a pure cysteine-pattern and size confusion, so a truly spurious false positive rather than a venom-recruited homolog.

Horned-viper venom-gland dimeric disintegrin CC8B, Toxin-keyworded integrin blocker; Disintegrin is its own modelled class, so calling M12B is the parent-fold confusion (disintegrins are proteolytically released from PII metalloproteinases).
Parasitoid-wasp venom-gland cysteine-rich venom protein 3 (knottin); venom-gland origin makes the tox call right, but UniProt assigns no family and nothing supports the Neurotoxin bin.
Cone-snail venom-duct O2 contryphan Vc1; harmless on intracranial injection into mice, but venom-duct origin governs, and the O2 superfamily maps onto Conotoxin family exactly.
Hornet venom-gland VESP-VB2, a Toxin-keyworded mast-cell degranulating mastoparan; MCD is both the label and the correct family, so the Formicidae venom call is an adjacent-aculeate family error.
Crab-spider venom-gland toxin Tbo-IT2, insecticidal (LD100 200 ug/g on housefly larvae); neurotoxin 02 (plectoxin) family maps onto Neurotoxin family exactly.
Wasp venom-gland Communis-AAAA, hemolytic (EC50 142.6 uM) and hyperalgesic in mice; MCD family (mastoparan subfamily) is exactly right.
Spider-wasp venom-gland fulvonin, a Toxin-keyworded bradykinin-related peptide targeting BDKRB1 and hyperalgesic in rats; model called nontox -> false negative, and on a family it does model.

Mosquito salivary aegyptin-like anti-platelet protein: a blood-feeder feeding secretion that blocks host collagen-platelet binding; model called nontox -> false negative. Same blind spot as the July alboserpin and tick TAP rows.
Red-headed-krait venom-gland acidic phospholipase A2 2; Phospholipase family is exactly right. Keyword gap on the label side, same as CE156.
Freshwater-pearl-mussel BPTI/Kunitz protein 5, a shell-matrix protein of the nacreous layer expressed in the mantle. Biomineralisation, not venom. Venom Kunitz call -> false positive.

Ant venom-gland M-poneritoxin-Nc3b, a Toxin-keyworded insecticidal ponericin (reversible paralysis in L.cuprina, PD50 26.4 nmol/g); model called nontox -> false negative. Note the model got the sister ponericin CE053 right.

Goat lactotransferrin, an endogenous iron-binding exocrine and immune protein. Model called 'other', a tox call, so this is the July duck-transferrin failure repeating on a second transferrin: the family is a genuine hard-negative pool.

Solitary-bee venom-gland macropin (the July lasioglossin precedent); UniProt bins it in the lasioglossin-like family, which is unmodeled, so 'other' was the right call and Cationic peptide is a specific wrong bin. Chemically defensible: macropin is a linear amphipathic melittin-like peptide.
Scorpion venom-gland toxin-like protein 14; venom-gland origin makes the tox call right, but UniProt assigns no family and Scoloptoxin is a centipede family.

Hornet venom-gland phospholipase A1 (Vesp v 1), a major vespid venom allergen with hemolytic activity. UniProt places it in the AB hydrolase/lipase family, which is unmodeled (the Phospholipase class only absorbs PLA2-type names), so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Saw-scaled-viper venom-gland dimeric disintegrin schistatin-like subunit B, Toxin-keyworded platelet-aggregation inhibitor; same Disintegrin versus M12B parent-fold confusion as CE166.
Scorpion venom-gland non-disulfide-bridged peptide 5.6, Toxin-keyworded, cytolytic and weakly hemolytic; model called nontox -> false negative, and on a family it does model.

Manduca sexta moricin, an insect innate-immunity AMP (the explicit July nontox precedent), with no hemolysis or cytotoxicity reported, so the hemolysis rule does not reach it. NDBP call -> false positive: AMP chemistry read as venom-peptide chemistry.
Scorpion venom-gland neurotoxin BmK A3-6; no effect on the channels tested, but venom-gland origin governs. UniProt assigns no family and short scorpion toxin superfamily is the taxon-standard bin.
Wasp venom-gland Polybia-CP, chemotactic and cytotoxic to HEK293 cells; MCD family (protonectin subfamily) is exactly right.

Bombina skin Maximins 3/H16: Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, and it encodes maximin-3, which is tumour-cytotoxic, anti-HIV and highly spermicidal. Both sibling precursors carrying the same maximin-3 (P83082, Q8JHE1) ARE Toxin-keyworded, so this nontox label is curator inconsistency. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Cape-cobra venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor 2; venom Kunitz-type is exactly right. Keyword gap on the label side.
